description: CTC-04's chamfered walls, read from STEP (blend-corners step 5): the part read in place and the foot of one chamfered wall filleted at the census's radius, the edge between a plane wall and its plane chamfer strip. At each end it runs on into a rounded corner, where the wall turns into a cylinder and the strip into a cone, at a vertex of four edges whose two other edges are tangent dihedrals as written but not as read: the normals across them are 7e-11 to 9e-10 apart, past the model's angular precision. A ball of the fillet's radius moved by that sine moves by under 1e-9, inside the faces' tolerance, so the faces are tangent for this blend and the chain walks on round the whole chamfered outline, twelve edges, each its own blend face: Open CASCADE's counts, 12 vertices, 24 edges and 12 faces more than the part's (ADR-0040); at 1e-12 alone it stopped there and the edge was refused VertexBlend. The file is not shrunk further (ADR-0026 §4); blend/chamfered-stadium-foot-fillet is the same corner built from a recipe. The desired body is Open CASCADE's

analytic.occt_walked: Open CASCADE's blend of a cylinder against a cone round each rounded corner is a B-spline surface walked along the edge, so its own STEP has NURBS faces beside the planes, the cylinders and the cones, whose pairs the checker's S5 leaves undecided
